objective_and_hypothesis.justification: This matches the score 2 description: the objective is clear, specific, and linked to mosquito sampling and whole-genome sequencing, but the paper does not state an explicit, testable hypothesis.
objective_and_hypothesis.quote: This study aims to investigate WNV circulation in mosquito populations from high-risk wetland areas in Portugal

public_health_relevance.justification: This matches the score 3 description because West Nile virus is presented as a recurrent human, animal, and wildlife health threat, and the study is explicitly contextualized by the major recent outbreaks in neighboring Spain.
public_health_relevance.quote: Since 2020, Spain has reported some of the largest WNV outbreaks in Europe

study_design_rigor.justification: This matches the score 3 description: the paper specifies sites, trap types, sampling dates, pooling, RT-qPCR confirmation, sequencing, bioinformatic thresholds, and phylogenetic workflow. Results were supported by sequencing confirmation and the reads and consensus genomes are reported as openly deposited.
study_design_rigor.quote: WNV reads generated in this study are deposited in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) under the BioProject PRJEB87871

results_and_conclusion.justification: This matches the score 2 description: Table 1, the text, and Figure 1 consistently support seven genomes and two lineage 1A clusters, while the discussion acknowledges genomic-surveillance limitations. However, the reported MIR percentages are tenfold too high given the stated positive-pool and mosquito totals: 7/3,706 is 0.19%, not 1.9%, and the site/species values similarly correspond to rates per 1,000 rather than percentages; this weakens the claim of relatively intense circulation.
results_and_conclusion.quote: Considering both sampling sites, the minimum infection rate (MIR) was estimated at 1.9%.

references.justification: The reference list provides a balanced set of foundational WNV studies, current peer-reviewed work on Iberian and European WNV epidemiology, vector ecology, sequencing, and surveillance methods, plus relevant software and data-platform citations. No clearly unrelated reference was identified.
references.quote: West Nile virus: an overview of its spread in Europe and the Mediterranean basin
